**[Root cause]** Since Spark 3.5, Hadoop-bundled Spark distributions deliberately stop propagating `yarn.application.classpath` and `mapreduce.application.classpath` to YARN-submitted applications, precisely to avoid transitive Guava/Jackson dependencies from the cluster clashing with Spark's bundled versions.

**[Version check]** The change takes effect from Spark 3.5 (not 3.1 as stated); verify with `spark-submit --version`, and check container launch logs for the missing classpath variables.

**[Repair steps]**
1. Restore old behavior: set the parameter related to `spark.hadoop.hadoopConf.yarn.app.classpath`, e.g. `--conf spark.hadoop.yarn.application.classpath="$HADOOP_CONF_DIR,..."` matching your cluster's configured classpath.
2. Or keep the default and instead shade Guava/Jackson in your job jar, or use `spark.driver/executor.userClassPathFirst=true` so app jars take precedence.
3. Relaunch and confirm no Guava/Jackson `NoSuchMethodError`.

[Root cause] `NoSuchMethodError` at RegionServer startup is a Hadoop/HBase version mismatch: HBase's compiled code calls Hadoop APIs that don't exist (or have different signatures) in the loaded Hadoop jar. [Version check] Run `hbase version` and `hadoop version`. The matrix lists supported Hadoop as 2.10.2+, 3.2.3+, 3.3.2–3.3.4, 3.3.5+, 3.4.0+; 3.1.0/3.1.1+ and 3.2.0–3.2.2 are incompatible.

[Repair steps] (1) Stop the cluster. (2) Upgrade Hadoop to ≥3.2.3 (preferably 3.3.5+). (3) Remove stale `hadoop-*` jars from HBase's lib/classpath. (4) Restart and confirm the versions match.

3. Alternatively, access the data from a 2.0+ cluster and export via ExportSnapshot/HBase copy, then bulkload into the target cluster.
4. Verify with an HFile scan on the 2.x reader.

5. Resubmit the job; YARN will auto-create .staging.

[Root cause] RegionTooBusyException means an HBase region is overloaded (hot-spot region) and rejects Spark read requests; balance and retry are needed on the HBase side.

3. Pre-split tables for high-ingest keys to prevent future hotspots.
4. Increase client retry settings (hbase.client.retries.number, rpc backoff) so Spark readers wait out busy regions.
5. Rerun the Spark 3.2 job and confirm reads succeed.
